Why do people generally (if it's a 12-hour day) rise after sun has risen but go to sleep when it has been already gone very dark for a few hours? Wouldn't it make more sense to use pre-sunrise light?

Before electricity became available in every home and along streets, people would wake and sleep in accordance to the sunrise and sunset. Obviously this is more sleep than most got. Many people would wake in the middle of the night and perform certain tasks by candlelight. Sometimes people would just fuck, cus what else is there to do?

Don't forget that today's modern light sources have all but destroyed our circadian rhythms. LED and fluorescent light has a very cool temperature, which your body usually associates with early morning.

People can wake, sleep, and do as they please with little regard for the 'sense' required by solar cycles, because we've got artificial light that's happy to do the job instead.

My theory is that people used to get up just before the sun ("We ride at dawn" was said before the age of alarm clocks) but busy days and the idea of a 'nightlife' make people push their activities later and later. We sleep in to compensate.

This current sleeping pattern is not actually our natural sleeping pattern. I read an article recently about sleeping patterns in human pre-fueled lights and it seems that we would go to sleep after sunset, wake up for a few hours in the middle of the night, return to sleep and then wake up around dawn.

This pattern is well documented in books from the middle ages that have prayers to be said in the interim period, sex positions to try, acitivities to do, snacks to eat, and so on. This pattern emerged only very recently and first in Northern European cities which were the first to be lit by gas and electric means.
